title: Never emit explicit null for unmentioned nullables where serde double_option lives
statement: With serde double_option columns, "absent" and "null" are OPPOSITES, and ts-rs flattens Option<Option<T>> to T|null, destroying the three-valued contract. Hand-write the update payload and assign nullable fields ONLY when the caller named them — the old builder emitted explicit null for every unmentioned nullable, which inverted to Some(None) when double_option arrived and any partial update wiped twelve columns. A regression test asserts the serialized payload HAS the key when explicitly null and LACKS it when omitted.

title: Make batching an explicit IPC-count decision with partial failure in the response
statement: Treat IPC call count as an explicit design decision: one detail call returns the whole aggregate with warnings?: string[] so partial success is reported, not thrown; bulk resolves carry a measured win; list projections stay lean with per-item rehydration; bulk deletes return per-id outcomes; and transactionality is pushed server-side to replace a two-IPC dance that could partially apply.

title: Let the api wrapper own wire casing and serialization
statement: The api wrapper owns wire casing and serialization: an explicit snake→camel adapter exported next to the raw call, wire-name-faithful interfaces where the backend renames, wrapper-owned JSON.stringify so callers pass objects, per-row key remapping at the boundary, and hand-written types where the generated binding is wrong (i64→bigint vs plain JSON numbers).

title: Coerce bigint to number only at a justified, explicit boundary
statement: bigint→number coercion happens at an explicit justified boundary: the raw wire is typed number|bigint, mapped with a typeof check, and each site argues why the value can't exceed 2^53; default fields the older backend may omit. The recorded opposite: a hand-rolled duplicate typing u64 as number DRIFTED — re-export the generated binding instead, and coerce at the seam only when you say why.

title: Type unions at the seam so invalid states are unreachable from TS
statement: Discriminated unions at the api seam mirror the backend match so invalid states are unreachable from TypeScript; the module ADR records that bridge hooks previously direct-invoked so the discriminator had no compile-time contract, and string-literal unions make typos surface at compile time instead of silently taking the else-branch.

title: Ship the client's UTC offset with every day-bucketed query
statement: Any backend aggregation that buckets by 'day' (SLA trends, health windows, daily uptime) should receive the caller's UTC offset (`-new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`) as a standard parameter so days align with the user's local calendar — otherwise a persona that fails every evening local time smears across two UTC days and the trend lies.

title: Serde casing attributes are wire contracts — pin them with a comment naming the consumers
statement: The field casing an event/IPC payload serializes with is a cross-boundary contract. A well-meaning cleanup that adds (or removes) `rename_all = "camelCase"` silently changes every key on the wire; untyped consumers read `undefined` and misbehave in ways far from the change. Pin the deliberate casing with a comment that names the exact consumer files and describes the failure a change would cause.

title: Creation flows must return the created id — never infer 'the newest row is mine'
statement: When a wizard/subflow creates an entity the parent flow must continue with, thread the created id through the completion callback explicitly. Inferring the created entity by max(created_at) is racy against concurrent creates and server-clock drift. After receiving the id, awaiting the list refresh is best-effort: the id alone is enough to render a minimal fallback, so a failed refresh must not abort the flow.

title: Adapt rows into the UI shape once; never let one row break the list
statement: When a stored row shape and the frontend model diverge, write one directional adapter that always returns a valid object: shape-tolerant field access, every nested JSON parse wrapped, unrecognised values falling to a documented default. A malformed row then degrades to a dull entry instead of blanking the whole catalog.

title: Move a 'refresh all' loop server-side into one privileged call
statement: A 'test all' button implemented as a client-side fan-out over N privileged calls creates a stampede that can race the very session-token injection those calls depend on, reporting healthy resources as failures. Put the loop behind one call that runs it in process, share that implementation with the scheduled sweep so both persist results identically, and accept an indeterminate progress bar as the price.

title: Close the outbound seam — the inbound one-door leaves it half done
statement: The inbound boundary is rigorously centralized while browser code calls the app's own routes from dozens of components, each re-implementing status branching, JSON parsing and error toasts. That asymmetry means the next contract change costs every component instead of one module.

title: Give the browser one typed request helper for your own routes
statement: Client components must reach the app's HTTP surface through a single request helper that owns timeouts, status-code branching and one typed error class, so callers branch on a named discriminator instead of re-deriving it from status codes. Per-component fetch with hand-rolled parsing and toasts is the same problem the inbound one-door already solved, left unfinished on the outbound side.

title: Reject out-of-window deliveries with 422 + Retry-After, and document the window on a GET
statement: An ingestion endpoint with an availability window should reject out-of-window deliveries with a retryable status (422) carrying a Retry-After header computed to the next window open, and expose a GET on the same route that reports window state without leaking internal metadata — so machine senders can back off correctly and humans can debug.

title: Wrap every route in one handler that owns errors and the envelope
statement: Response shape and error handling written per route drift into several dialects that every client must then understand. Wrap each route in one handler that catches thrown errors, logs them structurally, and coerces success and failure alike into a single typed envelope — the shape becomes a property of the layer rather than of whoever wrote the route.

title: Choose the entry-point form by caller identity, not convenience
statement: Internal UI mutations and external callers need different things: the former wants type safety and no public URL, the latter needs a stable URL and raw-request access for signature verification. Split on caller identity, write the decision table down, and standardize the file naming — when the rule is convention-only, greppable naming is the entire enforcement.

title: Pick one validation idiom and make the wrapper demand it
statement: Hand-written parse functions that return a value or null keep validation beside the route and add no dependency, at the cost of shared schema tooling and type inference; a schema library trades the reverse. Either is defensible — what matters is that the request wrapper takes the validator as a required option so no route can skip validation, and that the codebase does not run both idioms at once.
